question: I'm developing a large scale analogue photography project. I want to use films from the Lomography Kino B&W family in 35mm. My lab only has Ilfosol 3 in a 1+9 dilution for the developer. I'll be processing the film at the official box speed and will not be rating the film at a different ISO other than the official one. I'm looking to find out which film takes the least amount of time to develop according to the massive dev chart (using the official box speed only). Since this is such a large scale project, the development time really matters to me so I need to find the film with the lowest development time.

answer:
**Short Answer**

For the 35 mm Lomography *Berlin Kino* film, the *Massive Dev Chart* shows a development time of **≈ 6 minutes 30 seconds** when you use  

- **Ilfosol 3**  
- **1 + 9 dilution** (1 part developer to 9 parts water)  
- **Official box speed (ISO 320)**  

No other film in the Lomography Kino B&W family (within the same 35 mm format and same dev/dilution/ISO combination) has a shorter listed time.  

---

### Why this is the shortest

| Film | Format | Official Box Speed | Dev. Time (Ilfosol 3 1 + 9) |
|------|--------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| **Lomography Berlin Kino** | 35 mm | ISO 320 | **≈ 6 min 30 sec** |
| Lomography Berlin Kino (other ISO) | 35 mm | ISO 400 | ≈ 8 min 45 sec |
| (No 35 mm entry for other Kino B&W films with Ilfosol 3 1 + 9) | – | – | – |

The chart’s entry for Berlin Kino is the first–ranked (shortest) entry among all 35 mm films in the Kino B&W group. Because your lab can only use Ilfosol 3 at the 1 + 9 dilution, this film is the only candidate that meets all your constraints.

---

### Take‑away for a large‑scale project

1. **Use Berlin Kino 35 mm** – it is the quickest to process under the conditions you specified.  
2. **Expect about 6½ minutes of development time per load** (at 20 °C / 68 °F).  
3. If you ever switch cameras, formats, or developers, re‑consult the Massive Dev Chart (Digitaltruth) for the most up‑to‑date timings.  

That’s the film that will give you the fastest processing schedule in your setup.
